rankings.blurb: Four Cornerstones including the Drake Maye-Jahmyr Gibbs-Puka Nacua-Trey McBride nucleus that makes every other owner in this league physically ill. Yes, they mortgaged a boatload of picks to land Gibbs, and yes the pick cupboard is nearly bare, but when your floor is THIS high you don't need lottery tickets. The only knock is aging depth at RB and TE behind the starters, but Tetairoa McMillan and Carnell Tate are waiting in the wings. This is the class of the league and everyone else is playing for second.

Eleven Cornerstones and Foundational pieces — ELEVEN — and a WR room featuring Ja'Marr Chase, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, AND Drake London that should be illegal. Jayden Daniels and Justin Herbert as your QB1A and QB1B is genuinely disgusting. The recent trades are a little concerning — shipping off picks to nchernandez19 and losing value in the process — but when your roster is this loaded you can afford to leak a little oil. The zero-pick haul is the only thing keeping this team from the top spot; enjoy the ride, Sven, because the rest of us hate you.

Seven first-round picks and a total dynasty value north of 155K — Siny is the smartest rebuilder in the room and it's not particularly close. Caleb Williams and Jaxson Dart at QB is a future that makes you drool, and Jeremiyah Love plus Quinshon Judkins at RB is arguably the best young backfield in the league. The Trey McBride trade looks like a masterclass in asset management, turning a top TE into a mountain of future capital. This team isn't winning right now, but in two years everyone else will be apologizing.

Josh Allen at 9,998 KTC is the single most valuable player in this entire league, and pairing him with Ashton Jeanty is the kind of flex that makes you insufferable at the draft table. The WR corps of Garrett Wilson, Zay Flowers, and Jaylen Waddle is solidly Foundational across the board, but none of them are elite enough to carry a week alone. The recent trade flipping Tyler Shough for Baker Mayfield was a lateral move dressed up as a win, and the TE room behind Sam LaPorta is genuinely embarrassing. This team is one elite WR acquisition away from being a real threat.

Joe Burrow and Amon-Ra St. Brown are a legitimate Cornerstone duo, and picking up Jalen Hurts in that Akracoon deal looks like highway robbery in hindsight. But this team just got COOKED by nchernandez19 — shipping Jameson Williams and two future firsts for Malik Willis and Michael Wilson is the kind of trade that gets you mocked at the family dinner table. Zero first-round picks remaining and a RB room built around aging veterans Jonathan Taylor and Breece Hall is a ticking clock. The window is open but the frame is rotting.

Bijan Robinson and Brock Bowers is a Cornerstone pairing that would make any dynasty manager blush, and this team has been absolutely RAPING the trade market lately — fleecing GiantHawkTua and SvenMoney34 in back-to-back deals to stack six first-round picks. The QB situation is a dumpster fire though: Jordan Love, C.J. Stroud, and Geno Smith walk into a bar and none of them can win you a playoff game. Six future firsts means the upside is massive, but right now this roster is carrying a lot of 'maybe' at crucial positions. The glow-up is coming, but you're not eating steak yet.

Justin Jefferson and CeeDee Lamb are two of the best dynasty WRs alive and this team is absolutely wasting them. The RB room is CMC's knee injury away from a full collapse, and your QB trio of Purdy, Goff, and Darnold reads like a depth chart for a team that gave up. One first-round pick, no meaningful future capital, and a TE room headlined by Brenton Strange — BRENTON STRANGE — is the stuff of nightmares. This team needs to either sell the aging veterans and pivot to a full rebuild or go all-in at the deadline, because this 'sorta contending' limbo is the dynasty equivalent of death.

Lamar Jackson AND Patrick Mahomes in the same dynasty lineup is the most unhinged quarterback flex in this league, and yet somehow this team is sitting at rank 8 — because having two elite QBs doesn't mean much when your RB room is Derrick Henry's arthritic knees and Josh Jacobs. Zero future picks. None. Not a single dart throw at the future, which means when A.J. Brown and Tee Higgins age out there is absolutely nothing coming. The Ladd McConkey buy cost a 2028 first and Jalen Coker, which is a steep price for a WR2 on a team with no runway. Gorgeous starting lineup, catastrophic dynasty outlook.

Seth won the Gibbs trade and has been collecting picks like Infinity Stones, but let's be honest — this roster is a mess right now. Tyler Shough, Aaron Rodgers, and Quinn Ewers at QB is a crime against fantasy football, and George Pickens is your only legitimate Foundational piece on the player side. Five first-round picks is promising, and Travis Hunter could be a revelation, but right now you're asking Jadarian Price and TreVeyon Henderson to carry a contender and that's just not happening. There's a real team buried in here somewhere — call us in 2027.

You traded Ja'Marr Chase — CHASE — and the best thing you have to show for it is Fernando Mendoza and a pile of mid-round picks. Malik Nabers is a legitimate Cornerstone but he's the only one, and your QB room of Mendoza, Dak Prescott, and J.J. McCarthy is somehow the most depressing sentence in this entire document. Seven first-round picks sounds great until you realize your current roster can't win a single week of the season, meaning you're going to be stockpiling top-10 picks for the foreseeable future. The chili in Cincinnati is great; this rebuild, much like Skyline's hot takes, is going to take some time to develop.
